- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- claude-in-chrome: Automates your Chrome browser to interact with web pages - clicking elements, filling forms, capturing screenshots, reading console logs, and navigating sites. Opens pages in new tabs within your existing Chrome session. Requires site-level permissions before executing (configured in the extension). - When the user wants to interact with web pages, automate browser tasks, capture screenshots, read console logs, or perform any browser-based actions. Always invoke BEFORE attempting to use any mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

content.content:
stages:
  convert_labeled_data:
    cmd: python src/convert_labeled_data.py
    deps:
    - data/labeled_data.csv
    - src/convert_labeled_data.py
    outs:
    - data/annotation_per_row_data.csv
  fetch_labeled_data:
    cmd: ./src/fetch_data.sh
    deps:
    - src/fetch_data.sh
    outs:
    - data/labeled_data.csv
  download_audio:
    cmd: python ./src/download_audio.py --target-dir data/audio --annotations-file
      data/annotation_per_row_data.csv
    deps:
    - data/annotation_per_row_data.csv
    - src/download_audio.py
    outs:
    - data/audio:
        persist: true
  extract_data_quality:
    cmd: python ./src/extract_data_quality.py
    deps:
    - data/annotation_per_row_data.csv
    - src/extract_data_quality.py
    outs:
    - data/data_quality/sample_based_quality.json
    - data/data_quality/samples_per_label.csv
  fetch_noise_esc50:
    cmd: python src/fetch_noise_esc50.py
    deps:
    - src/fetch_noise_esc50.py
    - src/noise_pool.py
    params:
    - noise_pools.esc50
    outs:
    - data/noise/esc50

  fetch_noise_demand:
    cmd: python src/fetch_noise_demand.py
    deps:
    - src/fetch_noise_demand.py
    - src/noise_pool.py
    params:
    - noise_pools.demand
    outs:
    - data/noise/demand

  augmentation:
    cmd: python src/augment_data.py
    deps:
    - data/audio
    - data/noise/esc50
    - data/noise/demand
    - data/annotation_per_row_data.csv
    - src/augment_data.py
    params:
    - chunk_size
    - chunk_overlap
    - augmentation
    outs:
    - data/augmented_audio
    - data/augmented_annotations.csv

  extract_features:
    cmd: python src/extract_logmel_features.py
    deps:
    - data/audio
    - data/augmented_audio
    - data/noise/esc50
    - data/noise/demand
    - src/extract_logmel_features.py
    params:
    - feature_extraction
    - augmentation.external_noise_pools
    outs:
    - data/logmel_data/

  draw_data:
    cmd: python src/draw_data.py
    params:
    - inbalance_ratio
    - external_background_ratio
    - chunk_size
    - chunk_overlap
    - augmentation.external_noise_pools
    # features_dir/hop_length/type drive where and how chunks are sliced
    - feature_extraction
    deps:
    - data/annotation_per_row_data.csv
    - data/augmented_annotations.csv
    - data/logmel_data/
    - data/noise/esc50
    - data/noise/demand
    - src/draw_data.py
    outs:
    - data/balanced_data.h5
    - data/data_quality/chunk_balanced_quality.json
    - data/data_quality/chunks_per_label.csv

  train_model:
    cmd: python src/train_cnn.py
    deps:
    - data/balanced_data.h5
    - data/data_quality/sample_based_quality.json
    - data/data_quality/samples_per_label.csv
    - data/data_quality/chunk_balanced_quality.json
    - data/data_quality/chunks_per_label.csv
    - src/train_cnn.py
    - src/train_xgboost.py
    params:
    - model
    - training
    outs:
    - models/cnn_model.keras
    - models/cnn_normalization.npz

metrics:
- data/data_quality/sample_based_quality.json
- data/data_quality/chunk_balanced_quality.json
plots:
- number of samples vs label:
    template: bar_horizontal_sorted
    x: '0'
    y:
      data/data_quality/samples_per_label.csv: label
params:
- params.yaml
===PARAMS===
chunk_size: 2000 # ms
chunk_overlap: 250 #ms
inbalance_ratio: 1.0 # How much more background samples should be drawn
# Share of the drawn background chunks that comes from the external noise
# pools instead of the labeled recordings. If one source can't fill its
# share (e.g. inbalance_ratio > 1 exhausts the real background chunks),
# the other tops it up.
external_background_ratio: 0.5

augmentation:
  # Target signal-to-noise ratios (dB) for synthetic front_doorbell samples,
  # doorbell = signal, everything else = noise. Spans deeply buried (-15dB)
  # to clearly audible (+15dB) to cover realistic in-the-wild conditions.
  # The -15/-10 levels exist to break a metric ceiling: on the -5..15 sweep
  # every feature variant scored val_f1 1.0 on a ~230-chunk fold, which
  # can't separate them. At -15dB the bell sits ~32x below the noise in
  # power -- hard but still tractable from its narrowband harmonics, where
  # -20dB would be closer to unlabelable. Relies on the bell-like ESC-50
  # classes staying excluded (see noise_pools.esc50): with those in the
  # pool, a noise-dominated mix labeled front_doorbell would teach the
  # model that any bell is the doorbell.
  snrs_db: [-15, -10, -5, 0, 5, 10, 15]
  # How many random noise chunks to pair with each real doorbell chunk, per SNR
  pairs_per_signal_chunk: 2
  # Uniform loudness jitter (+/- dB) applied to each mixed sample so synthetic
  # positives vary in absolute level, not just SNR
  gain_jitter_db: 6
  # External noise pools (prepared by the fetch_noise_* stages). Per mix the
  # pool is chosen uniformly first, then a window within it, so the small
  # labeled-background pool isn't drowned out by these much larger ones.
  external_noise_pools:
    - data/noise/esc50
    - data/noise/demand

noise_pools:
  esc50:
    # Bell-like classes are excluded: at the low end of the SNR sweep the
    # noise dominates the mixture, and a mostly-bell sample labeled
    # front_doorbell would teach the model that other bells are doorbells.
    exclude_categories: [church_bells, clock_alarm]
  demand:
    # Domestic environments plus a hallway — closest to the deployed setting.
    # Other options: OOFFICE, OMEETING, PCAFETER, PRESTO, PSTATION, TBUS,
    # TCAR, TMETRO, SPSQUARE, STRAFFIC, SCAFE, NFIELD, NPARK, NRIVER
    environments: [DKITCHEN, DLIVING, DWASHING, OHALLWAY]

# Log-mel filterbank energies instead of MFCCs (this branch's experiment).
# Geometry deliberately mirrors the cnn-mfcc baseline -- same n_fft, same
# librosa-default hop of 512 (62 frames per 2000 ms chunk), same number of
# bands as n_mfcc was -- so the only thing that changes between the two runs
# is the missing DCT. Bump n_mels to widen the filterbank afterwards.
feature_extraction:
  type: logmel
  features_dir: ./data/logmel_data
  n_mels: 13
  n_fft: 512 # 32 ms @ 16 kHz
  hop_length: 512 # librosa.feature.mfcc default, kept for chunk-geometry parity
  # librosa.feature.mfcc's own mel filterbank defaults: full 0..sr/2 band
  fmin: 0
  fmax: null
  log_offset: 1.0e-6

training:
  test_size: 0.2

model:
  learning_rate: 0.001
  batch_size: 32
  epochs: 100
  early_stopping_patience: 10
  dropout: 0.3
  # MFCCs are already log-domain; raw STFT magnitudes are not (see
  # train_cnn.py) — flip this on the spectrogram branch
  log_compress: false
  random_state: 42

  # External noise pools (prepared by the fetch_noise_* stages). Per mix the
  # pool is chosen uniformly first, then a window within it, so the small
  # labeled-background pool isn't drowned out by these much larger ones.
  external_noise_pools:
    - data/noise/esc50
    - data/noise/demand

noise_pools:
  esc50:
    # Bell-like classes are excluded: at the low end of the SNR sweep the
    # noise dominates the mixture, and a mostly-bell sample labeled
    # front_doorbell would teach the model that other bells are doorbells.
    exclude_categories: [church_bells, clock_alarm]
  demand:
    # Domestic environments plus a hallway — closest to the deployed setting.
    # Other options: OOFFICE, OMEETING, PCAFETER, PRESTO, PSTATION, TBUS,
    # TCAR, TMETRO, SPSQUARE, STRAFFIC, SCAFE, NFIELD, NPARK, NRIVER
    environments: [DKITCHEN, DLIVING, DWASHING, OHALLWAY]

# Log-mel filterbank energies instead of MFCCs (this branch's experiment).
# Geometry deliberately mirrors the cnn-mfcc baseline -- same n_fft, same
# librosa-default hop of 512 (62 frames per 2000 ms chunk), same number of
# bands as n_mfcc was -- so the only thing that changes between the two runs
# is the missing DCT. Bump n_mels to widen the filterbank afterwards.
feature_extraction:
  type: logmel
  features_dir: ./data/logmel_data
  n_mels: 13
  n_fft: 512 # 32 ms @ 16 kHz
  hop_length: 512 # librosa.feature.mfcc default, kept for chunk-geometry parity
  # librosa.feature.mfcc's own mel filterbank defaults: full 0..sr/2 band
  fmin: 0
  fmax: null
  log_offset: 1.0e-6

training:
  test_size: 0.2

model:
  learning_rate: 0.001
  batch_size: 32
  epochs: 100
  early_stopping_patience: 10
  dropout: 0.3
  # MFCCs are already log-domain; raw STFT magnitudes are not (see
  # train_cnn.py) — flip this on the spectrogram branch
  log_compress: false
  random_state: 42

lastPrompt: compare the dags across all branches. how may it be possible to improve them?

content.text:
I have the full picture. Here's the comparison.

## DAG topology across branches

Eight branches carry a `dvc.yaml`. Seven of them have the **identical 10-stage DAG**; only two nodes differ.

| Branch | `extract_features` | `train_model` | extra | vs main |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `main` | `extract_mfcc_features.py` | `train_xgboost.py` | — | — |
| `cnn-mfcc` | mfcc | `train_cnn.py` | — | +1 |
| `stft-spectrogram-features` | `extract_stft_features.py` | xgboost | — | +9 |
| `cnn-spectrogram` | stft | cnn | — | +12 |
| `yamnet-features` | `extract_yamnet_features.py` | xgboost | — | +2 |
| `cnn-logmel` | `extract_logmel_features.py` | cnn | — | +5 |
| `esp32-logmel` | logmel | cnn | **`export_model`** (TFLite int8) | +13 |
| `tree-num-experiments` | mfcc | xgboost | *different shape* | stale (Jan 2025) |

`tree-num-experiments` is the only real topological outlier: it has `cut_in_chunks` + `balance_data_set` where everything else has `augmentation` + `draw_data`, and no noise-pool stages at all. It's an 18-month-old ancestor, not a live variant.

Everything else is **one DAG with two swapped commands**. The `fetch_*` → `convert` → `download` → `augment` → `draw` → `train` spine is byte-identical across all seven.

## The headline problem: the comparison is currently invalid

Comparing `dvc.lock` output hashes for the shared upstream stages:

```
main, cnn-mfcc, cnn-spectrogram, yamnet, stft, esp32-logmel:  aug=d5e03769
cnn-logmel:                                                   aug=47e945cf
```

Six branches trained on one dataset; `cnn-logmel` trained on a different one. The `-15/-10 dB` SNR extension (commit `c27dec5`) rewrote `augmentation`, and therefore everything downstream. So the recorded leaderboard — esp32-logmel 1.0 > yamnet 0.9956 > cnn-mfcc 0.9913 > cnn-spectrogram 0.9826 — is all on the **old, saturated `-5..15` sweep**, and the one branch on the new sweep has nothing to compare against. The metric ceiling you extended the sweep to break is still unbroken for every variant except one.

That's not a DAG design flaw so much as the predictable cost of branch-per-variant: a change to a shared upstream node silently desynchronizes the fleet, and nothing in the tooling tells you.

## How to improve them

**1. Collapse the fleet into a parameter axis.** Since only `extract_features` and `train_model` vary, this is a matrix, not seven branches. `draw_data.py` on `cnn-logmel` is already fully parametrized (`features_dir`/`hop_length`/`type` from params) — that generalization work is done, it just hasn't propagated back. Merge it, unify the four extractors into one `extract_features.py` dispatching on `feature_extraction.type` (mfcc vs logmel differ by ~15 real lines; the rest is duplicated boilerplate), and drive variants with `dvc exp run -S feature_extraction.type=... -S model.head=...`. One lock lineage, shared upstream cache, comparable by construction. Caveat: YAMNet won't fit the generic slicer — it needs mean-pooling over 480 ms hops rather than fixed-rate slicing, so it stays a genuine branch in the dispatch.

**2. Content-address the feature directories.** Both logmel branches write to `data/logmel_data` with *different geometry* (13 bands @ hop 512 vs 40 bands @ hop 320). The `data/logmel_data.esp32bak` (98 MB) sitting in your working tree is the manual workaround for exactly this collision, as is the untracked `data/stft_data/` left over from a branch switch. Key the directory on the feature params — `data/features/logmel-40x320/` — and variants coexist instead of clobbering each other.

**3. Stop extracting features for the whole noise pool.** `extract_features` runs over all 1,924 ESC-50 + DEMAND files, and `draw_data` then samples ~442 external background chunks from them (885 background total × `external_background_ratio` 0.5). Roughly 69% of the emitted `.npy` files exist to serve chunks that are mostly discarded — cheap at 29 MB for log-mel, but that's the **769 MB `data/stft_data`** on the spectrogram branches, per variant. Moving the noise-pool sampling *before* extraction (draw the chunk list, then extract only those windows) cuts the most expensive stage by ~3–4× and makes the STFT variants tractable to re-run.

**4. Promote `export_model` to the shared DAG.** It's the only genuine topology difference among live branches, and it's the stage that actually gates deployment. Its `max_f1_drop: 0.01` quantization check is a real correctness gate that six branches don't run. If ESP32-S3 is the committed target, every feature variant should be scored *after* int8 quantization, not before — a variant that wins in float32 and collapses in int8 is the wrong winner.

**5. Note on the "behind main" counts:** `esp32-logmel`, `cnn-spectrogram`, and `stft-spectrogram-features` all read as 6 commits behind, but their `dvc.yaml` already contains the noise-pool stages and their augmentation hash matches main's. The content arrived by duplicate/cherry-picked commits, so the git distance is history noise, not a content gap. Worth cleaning up before merging anything, since it makes `git log` comparisons untrustworthy.

The ordering I'd suggest: fix #1 and #2 together (they're the same refactor), re-run all variants once on the `-15 dB` sweep to restore a valid leaderboard, then #3 if the STFT re-runs prove painful.

"""
This script is to draw the data from the bigger dataset. It also takes care about data balancing.
"""

import json
import pandas as pd
import yaml
import numpy as np
from pathlib import Path
from pydub.utils import mediainfo
from dataqualityutils import get_data_quality_metrics
from tqdm import tqdm
from pandarallel import pandarallel


AUDIO_FILE_BASE = Path('./data/audio')
AUGMENTED_AUDIO_FILE_BASE = Path('./data/augmented_audio')
NOISE_POOL_FILE_BASE = Path('./data/noise')
SAMPLING_RATE = 16000


def resolve_audio_path(audio_file_name: str) -> Path:
    """Real annotations point at data/audio; augmented (mixed) samples live
    under data/augmented_audio; external noise pool files under
    data/noise/<pool>."""
    bases = [AUDIO_FILE_BASE, AUGMENTED_AUDIO_FILE_BASE]
    bases += sorted(d for d in NOISE_POOL_FILE_BASE.glob('*') if d.is_dir())
    for base in bases:
        candidate = base / audio_file_name
        if candidate.exists():
            return candidate
    raise FileNotFoundError(audio_file_name)


def external_background_rows(pool_dirs: list[str]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """One full-file background annotation row per external noise pool file,
    mirroring the tag-only convention of real background rows (no end time;
    the real file duration is filled in later). The pool name is kept in
    noise_pool so balancing can draw real and external background separately.
    """
    rows = []
    for pool_path in pool_dirs:
        pool_path = Path(pool_path)
        for wav_path in sorted(pool_path.glob('*.wav')):
            rows.append(
                {
                    "annotation_id": f"noise_{pool_path.name}_{wav_path.stem}",
                    "file_id": f"noise_{pool_path.name}_{wav_path.stem}",
                    "start": 0.0,
                    "end": np.nan,
                    "label": "background",
                    "audio_file_name": wav_path.name,
                    "remote_audio_path": "",
                    "noise_pool": pool_path.name,
                }
            )
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


def split_background_draw(
    n_target: int, external_ratio: float, n_real_available: int, n_external_available: int
) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """How many background chunks to draw from real recordings vs the
    external noise pools. external_ratio is the desired external share; if
    one source can't fill its share (e.g. inbalance_ratio > 1 exhausts the
    real background chunks), the other tops it up.
    """
    n_external = int(round(n_target * external_ratio))
    n_real = n_target - n_external

    if n_real > n_real_available:
        n_real = n_real_available
        n_external = min(n_target - n_real, n_external_available)
    elif n_external > n_external_available:
        n_external = n_external_available
        n_real = min(n_target - n_external, n_real_available)

    return n_real, n_external

def get_features(
    start: int, end: int, audio_file_name: str, features_dir: Path, frames_per_ms: float
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Reads out the time-frequency features from the file and cuts them
    according to start and end.

    Args:
        start (int): start in ms
        end (int): end in ms
        audio_file_name (str): file to read the features from
        features_dir (Path): directory holding the per-file .npy features
        frames_per_ms (float): sample_rate / hop_length / 1000 of the
            extractor that produced them

    Returns:
        np.ndarray: features interval according to start and end

def resolve_audio_path(audio_file_name: str) -> Path:
    """Real annotations point at data/audio; augmented (mixed) samples live
    under data/augmented_audio; external noise pool files under
    data/noise/<pool>."""
    bases = [AUDIO_FILE_BASE, AUGMENTED_AUDIO_FILE_BASE]
    bases += sorted(d for d in NOISE_POOL_FILE_BASE.glob('*') if d.is_dir())
    for base in bases:
        candidate = base / audio_file_name
        if candidate.exists():
            return candidate
    raise FileNotFoundError(audio_file_name)


def external_background_rows(pool_dirs: list[str]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """One full-file background annotation row per external noise pool file,
    mirroring the tag-only convention of real background rows (no end time;
    the real file duration is filled in later). The pool name is kept in
    noise_pool so balancing can draw real and external background separately.
    """
    rows = []
    for pool_path in pool_dirs:
        pool_path = Path(pool_path)
        for wav_path in sorted(pool_path.glob('*.wav')):
            rows.append(
                {
                    "annotation_id": f"noise_{pool_path.name}_{wav_path.stem}",
                    "file_id": f"noise_{pool_path.name}_{wav_path.stem}",
                    "start": 0.0,
                    "end": np.nan,
                    "label": "background",
                    "audio_file_name": wav_path.name,
                    "remote_audio_path": "",
                    "noise_pool": pool_path.name,
                }
            )
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


def split_background_draw(
    n_target: int, external_ratio: float, n_real_available: int, n_external_available: int
) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """How many background chunks to draw from real recordings vs the
    external noise pools. external_ratio is the desired external share; if
    one source can't fill its share (e.g. inbalance_ratio > 1 exhausts the
    real background chunks), the other tops it up.
    """
    n_external = int(round(n_target * external_ratio))

     3	(real recordings, augmented mixes, external noise pools), written as

    38	    model emits at least one frame instead of an empty embedding array."""
    39	    if len(waveform) >= min_samples:

    41	    return np.pad(waveform, (0, min_samples - len(waveform)))

C array in models/doorbell_model_data.cc (compiled into the firmware), and

    with open("params.yaml", "r") as file:

    export_params = params["export"]

    # (n, n_mels, n_frames, 1) here.
    X, y, le, feature_type, groups = load_dataset(params)
    train_idx, test_idx, _ = prepare_split(

    y_train, y_test = y[train_idx], y[test_idx]

    float_pred = (float_scores > 0.5).astype(int)
    float_metrics = compute_metrics(y_test, float_pred, "float_val")

    n_rep = min(export_params["representative_samples"], len(X_train))
    representative = X_train[rng.choice(len(X_train), n_rep, replace=False)]

    tflite_model = convert_int8(export_model, representative)

    int8_scores = tflite_predict(tflite_model, X_test)
    int8_pred = (int8_scores > 0.5).astype(int)
    int8_metrics = compute_metrics(y_test, int8_pred, "int8_val")

    # metric that will actually move first if a future retrain degrades.
    score_deviation = np.abs(float_scores - int8_scores)

    print(f"int8  val F1  : {int8_f1:.4f}  (drop {f1_drop:+.4f})")
    print(f"label agree   : {agreement:.4f}")
    print(f"score dev     : max {max_score_deviation:.4f}  mean {mean_score_deviation:.4f}")
    print(f"tflite size   : {len(tflite_model) / 1024:.1f} KB")
    print(f"peak tensor   : {peak_activation / 1024:.1f} KB")

        )

content.text: Porting done. Now the core restructure — first the shared audio-source module:

input.content:
"""Where the pipeline's audio comes from, and how a bare filename resolves.

Three sources feed the same flat namespace: labeled recordings
(data/audio), synthetic SNR mixes from the augmentation stage
(data/augmented_audio), and the external noise pools (data/noise/<pool>).
Filenames are unique across all three -- ESC-50 fold-id clips, DEMAND
<ENV>_ch01 and aug_* names don't collide with uploaded recordings -- so
downstream stages carry only `audio_file_name` and resolve it here.
"""

from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

AUDIO_FILE_BASE = Path("./data/audio")
AUGMENTED_AUDIO_FILE_BASE = Path("./data/augmented_audio")
NOISE_POOL_FILE_BASE = Path("./data/noise")

SAMPLING_RATE = 16000  # project-wide convention, see CLAUDE.md


def audio_search_bases() -> list[Path]:
    bases = [AUDIO_FILE_BASE, AUGMENTED_AUDIO_FILE_BASE]
    bases += sorted(d for d in NOISE_POOL_FILE_BASE.glob("*") if d.is_dir())
    return bases


def resolve_audio_path(audio_file_name: str) -> Path:
    """Real annotations point at data/audio; augmented (mixed) samples live
    under data/augmented_audio; external noise pool files under
    data/noise/<pool>."""
    for base in audio_search_bases():
        candidate = base / audio_file_name
        if candidate.exists():
            return candidate
    raise FileNotFoundError(audio_file_name)


def external_background_rows(pool_dirs: list[str]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """One full-file background annotation row per external noise pool file,
    mirroring the tag-only convention of real background rows (no end time;
    the real file duration is filled in later). The pool name is kept in
    noise_pool so balancing can draw real and external background separately.
    """
    rows = []
    for pool_path in pool_dirs:
        pool_path = Path(pool_path)
        for wav_path in sorted(pool_path.glob("*.wav")):
            rows.append(
                {
                    "annotation_id": f"noise_{pool_path.name}_{wav_path.stem}",
                    "file_id": f"noise_{pool_path.name}_{wav_path.stem}",
                    "start": 0.0,
                    "end": np.nan,
                    "label": "background",
                    "audio_file_name": wav_path.name,
                    "remote_audio_path": "",
                    "noise_pool": pool_path.name,
                }
            )
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

content.text: Now the feature registry — extraction *and* slicing per type, so `draw_data` stays thin:

input.content:
"""One registry for every feature representation the pipeline can build.

Previously each representation was its own script on its own branch
(extract_mfcc_features.py, extract_stft_features.py, ...), which were ~90%
identical boilerplate around a ~10-line transform, and each shipped a
matching hand-edited slicer inside draw_data.py. Both halves live here
instead, keyed by `feature_extraction.type`, so a variant is a parameter
rather than a branch.

Each entry owns three things:

* `params` -- which keys it reads out of the `feature_extraction` block,
  so the sidecar config (and therefore the DVC param hash) contains exactly
  what affects the output and nothing else.
* `extract` -- file -> (n_bins, n_frames) float array.
* `slice_chunk` -- how draw_data.py cuts a [start_ms, end_ms) window out of
  that array. This is per-type because it is not always a fixed frame rate
  (see yamnet below).
"""

import json
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Callable

import numpy as np

from audio_sources import SAMPLING_RATE

FEATURE_CONFIG_FILENAME = "feature_config.json"


def _load_mono_int16_scale(file_path: Path | str) -> tuple[np.ndarray, int]:
    """Audio as float32 at int16 amplitude scale, downmixed to mono.

    Mono matters: stereo files would double the sample count (interleaved)
    and break the frames-per-ms assumption the slicers rely on. int16 scale
    (rather than [-1, 1]) is kept because every extractor here has always
    used it, and normalization happens globally at training time.
    """
    from pydub import AudioSegment
    from pydub.utils import mediainfo

    audio = AudioSegment.from_wav(file_path)
    info = mediainfo(file_path)
    audio = audio.set_channels(1)
    samples = np.array(audio.get_array_of_samples(), dtype=np.float32)
    return samples, int(info["sample_rate"])


def extract_mfcc(file_path, n_mfcc: int, n_fft: int, hop_length: int) -> np.ndarray:
    import librosa

    samples, sample_rate = _load_mono_int16_scale(file_path)
    mfccs = librosa.feature.mfcc(
        y=samples, sr=sample_rate, n_mfcc=n_mfcc, n_fft=n_fft, hop_length=hop_length
    )
    return mfccs.astype(np.float32)


def extract_logmel(
    file_path,
    n_mels: int,
    n_fft: int,
    hop_length: int,
    fmin: int,
    fmax: int | None,
    log_offset: float,
) -> np.ndarray:

    MFCCs are log-mel energies run through a DCT, which decorrelates the
    bins so a tree sees compact, roughly independent features. A CNN does
    not want that: it wants the locally correlated structure along the
    frequency axis that the DCT destroys.

    The log is applied here rather than in the trainer, so params.yaml sets
    model.log_compress: false for this type and the .npy files are exactly
    what an on-device C frontend has to reproduce.
    """
    import librosa

    samples, sample_rate = _load_mono_int16_scale(file_path)
    mel = librosa.feature.melspectrogram(
        y=samples,
        sr=sample_rate,
        n_fft=n_fft,
        hop_length=hop_length,
        n_mels=n_mels,
        fmin=fmin,
        fmax=fmax,
    )

    # would additionally clip to top_db below the per-file peak, which is a
    # per-file operation we don't want ahead of a global normalization.
    return np.log(mel + log_offset).astype(np.float32)

    model.log_compress: true for this type so the trainer does it."""
    from scipy.signal import stft

    Deliberately NOT a per-file average rate (array.shape[1] / duration):
    the frame count carries a constant +1 offset, which is negligible for
    long real files (average rate ~= true rate) but dominant for exactly
    chunk_size-long augmented clips (average rate skews high). Per-file
    rates produced inconsistent chunk widths and broke np.vstack downstream.

    frames_per_ms = SAMPLING_RATE / cfg["hop_length"] / 1000

        slice_chunk=yamnet_slice,

        keeps_time_axis=False,
    ),

    try:

        raise SystemExit(
            f"unknown feature_extraction.type {feature_type!r}; "
            f"known types: {', '.join(sorted(REGISTRY))}"
        )


def extractor_config(feature_params: dict) -> dict:
    """The subset of feature_extraction that actually changes the output.

    `features_dir` is deliberately excluded: where the arrays are written
    does not affect what is in them, so moving the directory must not
    invalidate a cached extraction.
    """
    spec = get_spec(feature_params["type"])
    missing = [k for k in spec.params if k not in feature_params]
    if missing:
        raise SystemExit(
            f"feature_extraction.type {feature_params['type']!r} needs "
            f"missing param(s): {', '.join(missing)}"
        )
    config = {k: feature_params[k] for k in spec.params}
    config["type"] = feature_params["type"]
    return config

    config = extractor_config(feature_params)
    (features_dir / FEATURE_CONFIG_FILENAME).write_text(json.dumps(config, indent=4))


def verify_feature_config(features_dir: Path, feature_params: dict) -> dict:
    """Fail loudly when the .npy files on disk were built by a different
    configuration than the one currently in params.yaml.

    This is the guard for the failure that produced data/logmel_data.esp32bak:
    two branches wrote different geometry (13 bands @ hop 512 vs 40 @ hop 320)
    into the same directory name, and nothing downstream noticed until the
    shapes disagreed several stages later -- or worse, did not disagree.
    """
    expected = extractor_config(feature_params)
    config_path = features_dir / FEATURE_CONFIG_FILENAME

    if not config_path.exists():
        raise SystemExit(
            f"{config_path} is missing -- {features_dir} was not written by "
            f"extract_features.py. Re-run the extract_features stage."
        )

    actual = json.loads(config_path.read_text())
    if actual != expected:
        differing = sorted(
            set(actual) | set(expected), key=lambda k: (actual.get(k) == expected.get(k), k)
        )
        detail = "\n".join(
            f"  {k}: on disk {actual.get(k)!r} != params.yaml {expected.get(k)!r}"
            for k in differing
            if actual.get(k) != expected.get(k)
        )
        raise SystemExit(

        )

input.content:
"""Decide which audio chunks make up the training set -- before any features exist.

This is the first half of what draw_data.py used to do. Splitting it out buys
two things:

1. **Feature extraction stops being speculative.** It used to run over every
   file in every source, including all ~1900 external noise-pool files, and
   draw_data then sampled a few hundred background chunks out of that. Most
   of the extracted arrays were discarded -- cheap for log-mel, 769 MB for
   STFT. extract_features.py now reads this manifest and touches only the
   files a chunk actually references.

2. **Sampling is shared across feature variants.** Nothing here depends on
   `feature_extraction`, so switching representation (or sweeping n_mels)
   reuses this stage's cache instead of re-deciding the split. Every variant
   therefore trains on exactly the same chunks, which is what makes the
   MLflow comparison between them mean anything.

Output is data/chunk_manifest.csv, in final (shuffled) row order -- draw_data
just attaches features to it, so the ordering fed to the trainer is decided
here and only here.
"""

import json
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd
import yaml
from pandarallel import pandarallel
from pydub.utils import mediainfo
from tqdm import tqdm

from audio_sources import external_background_rows, resolve_audio_path
from dataqualityutils import get_data_quality_metrics

MANIFEST_PATH = Path("./data/chunk_manifest.csv")
DATA_QUALITY_DIR = Path("./data/data_quality")


def split_background_draw(
    n_target: int, external_ratio: float, n_real_available: int, n_external_available: int
) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """How many background chunks to draw from real recordings vs the
    external noise pools. external_ratio is the desired external share; if
    one source can't fill its share (e.g. inbalance_ratio > 1 exhausts the
    real background chunks), the other tops it up.
    """
    n_external = int(round(n_target * external_ratio))
    n_real = n_target - n_external

    if n_real > n_real_available:
        n_real = n_real_available
        n_external = min(n_target - n_real, n_external_available)
    elif n_external > n_external_available:
        n_external = n_external_available
        n_real = min(n_target - n_external, n_real_available)

    return n_real, n_external


def build_annotations(params: dict) -> pd.DataFrame:
    annotated_data = pd.read_csv("./data/annotation_per_row_data.csv")
    # Synthetic front_doorbell samples from the augmentation stage (mixed
    # signal+noise at target SNRs) are appended as regular rows so they flow
    # through the same chunking/balancing logic as real annotations.
    augmented_data = pd.read_csv("./data/augmented_annotations.csv")
    annotated_data = pd.concat([annotated_data, augmented_data], ignore_index=True)

    # External noise pool files (ESC-50, DEMAND) join as background rows so
    # the negative class also sees diverse non-Pi-mic noise, not just the
    # labeled recordings.
    external_data = external_background_rows(
        params["augmentation"]["external_noise_pools"]
    )
    annotated_data = pd.concat([annotated_data, external_data], ignore_index=True)

    # Group key for leakage-safe train/val splitting downstream: augmented rows
    # already carry the source file of their signal chunk; real rows (no
    # split_group column in their CSV) group by their own file. Overlapping
    # sliding windows and SNR variants of one recording thus share a group.
    annotated_data["split_group"] = annotated_data["split_group"].fillna(
        annotated_data["audio_file_name"]
    )
    return annotated_data


def cut_into_chunks(annotated_data: pd.DataFrame, chunk_size: int, chunk_overlap: int):
    return pd.DataFrame(
        [
            row.to_dict()
            | {"chunk_start": chunk_start, "chunk_end": (chunk_start + chunk_size)}
            for _, row in annotated_data.iterrows()
            for chunk_start in range(
                int(row["start"] * 1000),  # convert to ms
                int(row["end"] * 1000) - chunk_size,
                chunk_overlap,
            )
        ]
    )


def balance_chunks(chunks: pd.DataFrame, params: dict) -> pd.DataFrame:
    background_samples = chunks[chunks["label"] == "background"]
    # TODO try imputations
    non_background_samples = chunks[chunks["label"] != "background"]

    # Randomly sample from background class relative to the minority class
    # size (inbalance_ratio > 1 means more background than positives). Real
    # and external background are drawn separately so the huge external
    # pools can't crowd out the deployed-mic recordings.
    n_background_target = int(len(non_background_samples) * params["inbalance_ratio"])
    real_background = background_samples[background_samples["noise_pool"].isna()]
    external_background = background_samples[background_samples["noise_pool"].notna()]
    n_real, n_external = split_background_draw(
        n_background_target,
        params["external_background_ratio"],
        len(real_background),
        len(external_background),
    )
    if n_real + n_external < n_background_target:
        print(
            f"Warning: only {n_real + n_external} background chunks available, "
            f"target was {n_background_target}"
        )
    balanced_background = pd.concat(
        [
            real_background.sample(n=n_real, random_state=42),
            external_background.sample(n=n_external, random_state=42),
        ]
    )

    balanced_df = pd.concat([balanced_background, non_background_samples])
    # Shuffle here rather than downstream: this is the row order the trainer
    # ultimately sees, and it must not depend on the feature variant.
    return balanced_df.sample(frac=1, random_state=42).reset_index(drop=True)


def main():
    tqdm.pandas()
    pandarallel.initialize(progress_bar=True)

    with open("params.yaml", "r") as file:

"""Decide which audio chunks make up the training set -- before any features exist.

This is the first half of what draw_data.py used to do. Splitting it out buys
two things:

1. **Feature extraction stops being speculative.** It used to run over every
   file in every source, including all ~1900 external noise-pool files, and
   draw_data then sampled a few hundred background chunks out of that. Most
   of the extracted arrays were discarded -- cheap for log-mel, 769 MB for
   STFT. extract_features.py now reads this manifest and touches only the
   files a chunk actually references.

2. **Sampling is shared across feature variants.** Nothing here depends on
   `feature_extraction`, so switching representation (or sweeping n_mels)
   reuses this stage's cache instead of re-deciding the split. Every variant
   therefore trains on exactly the same chunks, which is what makes the
   MLflow comparison between them mean anything.

Output is data/chunk_manifest.csv, in final (shuffled) row order -- draw_data
just attaches features to it, so the ordering fed to the trainer is decided
here and only here.
"""

import json
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd
import yaml
from pandarallel import pandarallel
from pydub.utils import mediainfo
from tqdm import tqdm

from audio_sources import external_background_rows, resolve_audio_path
from dataqualityutils import get_data_quality_metrics

MANIFEST_PATH = Path("./data/chunk_manifest.csv")
DATA_QUALITY_DIR = Path("./data/data_quality")


def split_background_draw(
    n_target: int, external_ratio: float, n_real_available: int, n_external_available: int
) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """How many background chunks to draw from real recordings vs the
    external noise pools. external_ratio is the desired external share; if
    one source can't fill its share (e.g. inbalance_ratio > 1 exhausts the
    real background chunks), the other tops it up.
    """
    n_external = int(round(n_target * external_ratio))
    n_real = n_target - n_external

    if n_real > n_real_available:
        n_real = n_real_available
        n_external = min(n_target - n_real, n_external_available)
    elif n_external > n_external_available:
        n_external = n_external_available
        n_real = min(n_target - n_external, n_real_available)

    return n_real, n_external


def build_annotations(params: dict) -> pd.DataFrame:
    annotated_data = pd.read_csv("./data/annotation_per_row_data.csv")
    # Synthetic front_doorbell samples from the augmentation stage (mixed
    # signal+noise at target SNRs) are appended as regular rows so they flow
    # through the same chunking/balancing logic as real annotations.
    augmented_data = pd.read_csv("./data/augmented_annotations.csv")
    annotated_data = pd.concat([annotated_data, augmented_data], ignore_index=True)

    # External noise pool files (ESC-50, DEMAND) join as background rows so
    # the negative class also sees diverse non-Pi-mic noise, not just the
    # labeled recordings.
    external_data = external_background_rows(
        params["augmentation"]["external_noise_pools"]
    )
    annotated_data = pd.concat([annotated_data, external_data], ignore_index=True)

    # Group key for leakage-safe train/val splitting downstream: augmented rows
    # already carry the source file of their signal chunk; real rows (no
    # split_group column in their CSV) group by their own file. Overlapping
    # sliding windows and SNR variants of one recording thus share a group.
    annotated_data["split_group"] = annotated_data["split_group"].fillna(
        annotated_data["audio_file_name"]
    )
    return annotated_data


def cut_into_chunks(annotated_data: pd.DataFrame, chunk_size: int, chunk_overlap: int):
    return pd.DataFrame(
        [
            row.to_dict()
            | {"chunk_start": chunk_start, "chunk_end": (chunk_start + chunk_size)}
            for _, row in annotated_data.iterrows()
            for chunk_start in range(
                int(row["start"] * 1000),  # convert to ms
                int(row["end"] * 1000) - chunk_size,
                chunk_overlap,
            )
        ]
    )


def balance_chunks(chunks: pd.DataFrame, params: dict) -> pd.DataFrame:
    background_samples = chunks[chunks["label"] == "background"]
    # TODO try imputations
    non_background_samples = chunks[chunks["label"] != "background"]

    # Randomly sample from background class relative to the minority class
    # size (inbalance_ratio > 1 means more background than positives). Real
    # and external background are drawn separately so the huge external
    # pools can't crowd out the deployed-mic recordings.
    n_background_target = int(len(non_background_samples) * params["inbalance_ratio"])
    real_background = background_samples[background_samples["noise_pool"].isna()]
    external_background = background_samples[background_samples["noise_pool"].notna()]
    n_real, n_external = split_background_draw(
        n_background_target,
        params["external_background_ratio"],
        len(real_background),
        len(external_background),
    )
    if n_real + n_external < n_background_target:
        print(
            f"Warning: only {n_real + n_external} background chunks available, "
            f"target was {n_background_target}"
        )
    balanced_background = pd.concat(
        [
            real_background.sample(n=n_real, random_state=42),
            external_background.sample(n=n_external, random_state=42),
        ]
    )

    balanced_df = pd.concat([balanced_background, non_background_samples])
    # Shuffle here rather than downstream: this is the row order the trainer
    # ultimately sees, and it must not depend on the feature variant.
    return balanced_df.sample(frac=1, random_state=42).reset_index(drop=True)


def main():
    tqdm.pandas()
    pandarallel.initialize(progress_bar=True)

    with open("params.yaml", "r") as file:
        params = yaml.safe_load(file)

    annotated_data = build_annotations(params)

    # Preload duration, so we don't have to read the file for each chunk
    annotated_data["audio_file_duration"] = annotated_data[
        "audio_file_name"
    ].parallel_apply(lambda x: mediainfo(resolve_audio_path(x))["duration"])

    # Full-file background annotations (tag-only in Label Studio) carry no end
    # time; use the real file duration
    annotated_data["end"] = annotated_data["end"].fillna(
        annotated_data["audio_file_duration"].astype(float)
    )

    chunks = cut_into_chunks(
        annotated_data, params["chunk_size"], params["chunk_overlap"]
    )
    balanced_df = balance_chunks(chunks, params)

    DATA_QUALITY_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    balanced_df.groupby("label").size().to_csv(DATA_QUALITY_DIR / "chunks_per_label.csv")
    with open(DATA_QUALITY_DIR / "chunk_balanced_quality.json", "w") as f:
        json.dump(get_data_quality_metrics(balanced_df), f, indent=4)

    MANIFEST_PATH.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    balanced_df.to_csv(MANIFEST_PATH, index=False)

    n_files = balanced_df["audio_file_name"].nunique()
    print(f"{len(balanced_df)} chunks from {n_files} distinct files -> {MANIFEST_PATH}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Attach features to the chunks select_chunks.py already picked.

Everything about *which* chunks make up the dataset moved to
select_chunks.py; what is left here is purely "slice the arrays and write
the HDF5". That split is what lets one sampling decision be shared by every
feature variant.

The features column is named after the representation that produced it
(mfcc_features, logmel_features, ...) because train_cnn.py and
train_xgboost.py auto-detect the single *_features column and use its prefix
as the MLflow feature_type.
"""

from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import yaml
from pandarallel import pandarallel
from tqdm import tqdm

from features import get_spec, verify_feature_config
from select_chunks import MANIFEST_PATH

OUTPUT_PATH = Path("./data/balanced_data.h5")


def load_features(audio_file_name: str, features_dir: Path) -> np.ndarray:
    return np.load(features_dir / Path(audio_file_name).with_suffix(".npy").name)


def main():
    tqdm.pandas()
    pandarallel.initialize(progress_bar=True)

    with open("params.yaml", "r") as file:
        params = yaml.safe_load(file)

    feature_params = params["feature_extraction"]
    features_dir = Path(feature_params["features_dir"])
    feature_type = feature_params["type"]
    spec = get_spec(feature_type)

    # Refuse to slice arrays that were built by a different configuration
    # than the one in params.yaml right now.
    verify_feature_config(features_dir, feature_params)

    balanced_df = pd.read_csv(MANIFEST_PATH)

    features_column = f"{feature_type}_features"
    balanced_df[features_column] = balanced_df.parallel_apply(
        lambda row: spec.slice_chunk(
            load_features(row["audio_file_name"], features_dir),
            row["chunk_start"],
            row["chunk_end"],
            feature_params,
        ),
        axis=1,
    )

    shapes = {f.shape for f in balanced_df[features_column]}
    if len(shapes) != 1:
        raise SystemExit(
            f"inconsistent chunk shapes from {features_dir}: {sorted(shapes)}. "
            f"The trainer stacks these, so they must all agree."
        )

    OUTPUT_PATH.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    balanced_df.to_hdf(OUTPUT_PATH, key="data", index=False)
    print(f"{len(balanced_df)} chunks of shape {shapes.pop()} -> {OUTPUT_PATH}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Attach features to the chunks select_chunks.py already picked.

Everything about *which* chunks make up the dataset moved to
select_chunks.py; what is left here is purely "slice the arrays and write
the HDF5". That split is what lets one sampling decision be shared by every
feature variant.

The features column is named after the representation that produced it
(mfcc_features, logmel_features, ...) because train_cnn.py and
train_xgboost.py auto-detect the single *_features column and use its prefix
as the MLflow feature_type.
"""

from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import yaml
from pandarallel import pandarallel
from tqdm import tqdm

from features import get_spec, verify_feature_config
from select_chunks import MANIFEST_PATH

OUTPUT_PATH = Path("./data/balanced_data.h5")


def load_features(audio_file_name: str, features_dir: Path) -> np.ndarray:
    return np.load(features_dir / Path(audio_file_name).with_suffix(".npy").name)


def main():
    tqdm.pandas()
    pandarallel.initialize(progress_bar=True)

    with open("params.yaml", "r") as file:
        params = yaml.safe_load(file)

    feature_params = params["feature_extraction"]
    features_dir = Path(feature_params["features_dir"])
    feature_type = feature_params["type"]
    spec = get_spec(feature_type)

    # Refuse to slice arrays that were built by a different configuration
    # than the one params.yaml currently asks for.
    verify_feature_config(features_dir, feature_params)

    balanced_df = pd.read_csv(MANIFEST_PATH)

    features_column = f"{feature_type}_features"
    balanced_df[features_column] = balanced_df.parallel_apply(
        lambda row: spec.slice_chunk(
            load_features(row["audio_file_name"], features_dir),
            row["chunk_start"],
            row["chunk_end"],
            feature_params,
        ),
        axis=1,
    )

    shapes = {f.shape for f in balanced_df[features_column]}
    if len(shapes) != 1:
        raise SystemExit(
            f"inconsistent chunk shapes from {features_dir}: {sorted(shapes)}. "
            f"The trainer stacks these, so they all have to agree."
        )

    OUTPUT_PATH.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    balanced_df.to_hdf(OUTPUT_PATH, key="data", index=False)
    print(f"{len(balanced_df)} chunks of shape {shapes.pop()} -> {OUTPUT_PATH}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""
This script is to draw the data from the bigger dataset. It also takes care about data balancing.
"""

import json
import pandas as pd
import yaml
import numpy as np
from pathlib import Path
from pydub.utils import mediainfo
from dataqualityutils import get_data_quality_metrics
from tqdm import tqdm
from pandarallel import pandarallel


AUDIO_FILE_BASE = Path('./data/audio')
AUGMENTED_AUDIO_FILE_BASE = Path('./data/augmented_audio')
NOISE_POOL_FILE_BASE = Path('./data/noise')
SAMPLING_RATE = 16000


def resolve_audio_path(audio_file_name: str) -> Path:
    """Real annotations point at data/audio; augmented (mixed) samples live
    under data/augmented_audio; external noise pool files under
    data/noise/<pool>."""
    bases = [AUDIO_FILE_BASE, AUGMENTED_AUDIO_FILE_BASE]
    bases += sorted(d for d in NOISE_POOL_FILE_BASE.glob('*') if d.is_dir())
    for base in bases:
        candidate = base / audio_file_name
        if candidate.exists():
            return candidate
    raise FileNotFoundError(audio_file_name)


def external_background_rows(pool_dirs: list[str]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """One full-file background annotation row per external noise pool file,
    mirroring the tag-only convention of real background rows (no end time;
    the real file duration is filled in later). The pool name is kept in
    noise_pool so balancing can draw real and external background separately.
    """
    rows = []
    for pool_path in pool_dirs:
        pool_path = Path(pool_path)
        for wav_path in sorted(pool_path.glob('*.wav')):
            rows.append(
                {
                    "annotation_id": f"noise_{pool_path.name}_{wav_path.stem}",
                    "file_id": f"noise_{pool_path.name}_{wav_path.stem}",
                    "start": 0.0,
                    "end": np.nan,
                    "label": "background",
                    "audio_file_name": wav_path.name,
                    "remote_audio_path": "",
                    "noise_pool": pool_path.name,
                }
            )
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


def split_background_draw(
    n_target: int, external_ratio: float, n_real_available: int, n_external_available: int
) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """How many background chunks to draw from real recordings vs the
    external noise pools. external_ratio is the desired external share; if
    one source can't fill its share (e.g. inbalance_ratio > 1 exhausts the
    real background chunks), the other tops it up.
    """
    n_external = int(round(n_target * external_ratio))
    n_real = n_target - n_external

    if n_real > n_real_available:
        n_real = n_real_available
        n_external = min(n_target - n_real, n_external_available)
    elif n_external > n_external_available:
        n_external = n_external_available
        n_real = min(n_target - n_external, n_real_available)

    return n_real, n_external

def get_features(
    start: int, end: int, audio_file_name: str, features_dir: Path, frames_per_ms: float
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Reads out the time-frequency features from the file and cuts them
    according to start and end.

    Args:
        start (int): start in ms
        end (int): end in ms
        audio_file_name (str): file to read the features from
        features_dir (Path): directory holding the per-file .npy features
        frames_per_ms (float): sample_rate / hop_length / 1000 of the
            extractor that produced them

    Returns:
        np.ndarray: features interval according to start and end
    """

    features_file_path = features_dir / audio_file_name.replace('.wav', '.npy')
    spectrogram = np.load(features_file_path)

    # Use the fixed sample_rate/hop_length rate the extractor used to build
    # the array, not a per-file average (spectrogram.shape[1] / duration): the
    # frame count has a constant +1 offset, which is negligible for long
    # real files (avg rate ~= true rate) but dominant for exactly
    # chunk_size-long augmented clips (avg rate skews high), so per-file
    # rates produced inconsistent chunk widths and broke np.vstack downstream.
    start_sample = int(frames_per_ms * start)
    chunk_size = int(frames_per_ms * (end - start))
    end_sample = start_sample + chunk_size # This way the shape of the slice it more reliably the same every time

    res = spectrogram[:, start_sample:end_sample]

    return res

if __name__ == "__main__":
    
    tqdm.pandas()
    pandarallel.initialize(progress_bar=True)

    with open("params.yaml", "r") as file:
        params = yaml.safe_load(file)

    annotated_data = pd.read_csv("./data/annotation_per_row_data.csv")
    # Synthetic front_doorbell samples from the augmentation stage (mixed
    # signal+noise at target SNRs) are appended as regular rows so they flow
    # through the same chunking/balancing logic as real annotations.
    augmented_data = pd.read_csv("./data/augmented_annotations.csv")
    annotated_data = pd.concat([annotated_data, augmented_data], ignore_index=True)

    # External noise pool files (ESC-50, DEMAND) join as background rows so
    # the negative class also sees diverse non-Pi-mic noise, not just the
    # labeled recordings.
    external_data = external_background_rows(params["augmentation"]["external_noise_pools"])
    annotated_data = pd.concat([annotated_data, external_data], ignore_index=True)

    # Group key for leakage-safe train/val splitting downstream: augmented rows
    # already carry the source file of their signal chunk; real rows (no
    # split_group column in their CSV) group by their own file. Overlapping
    # sliding windows and SNR variants of one recording thus share a group.
    annotated_data["split_group"] = annotated_data["split_group"].fillna(
        annotated_data["audio_file_name"]
    )

    # Preload duration, so we don't have to read the file for each chunk
    annotated_data["audio_file_duration"] = annotated_data["audio_file_name"].parallel_apply(lambda x: mediainfo(resolve_audio_path(x))["duration"])

    # Full-file background annotations (tag-only in Label Studio) carry no end
    # time; use the real file duration
    annotated_data["end"] = annotated_data["end"].fillna(annotated_data["audio_file_duration"].astype(float))

    # Cut in chunks
    chunk_size = params["chunk_size"]
    chunk_overlap = params["chunk_overlap"]

    # Create chunks using list comprehension instead of iterative append
    chunks = [
        row.to_dict() | {"chunk_start": chunk_start, "chunk_end": (chunk_start + chunk_size)}
        for _, row in annotated_data.iterrows()
        for chunk_start in range(
            int(row["start"] * 1000),  # convert to ms
            int(row["end"] * 1000) - chunk_size,
            chunk_overlap,
        )
    ]
    chunks = pd.DataFrame(chunks)
    
    # Split into background and non-background samples
    background_samples = chunks[chunks["label"] == "background"]

    # TODO try imputations
    non_background_samples = chunks[chunks["label"] != "background"]

    # Randomly sample from background class relative to the minority class
    # size (inbalance_ratio > 1 means more background than positives). Real
    # and external background are drawn separately so the huge external
    # pools can't crowd out the deployed-mic recordings.
    n_background_target = int(len(non_background_samples) * params['inbalance_ratio'])
    real_background = background_samples[background_samples['noise_pool'].isna()]
    external_background = background_samples[background_samples['noise_pool'].notna()]
    n_real, n_external = split_background_draw(
        n_background_target,
        params['external_background_ratio'],
        len(real_background),
        len(external_background),
    )
    if n_real + n_external < n_background_target:
        print(
            f"Warning: only {n_real + n_external} background chunks available, "
            f"target was {n_background_target}"
        )
    balanced_background = pd.concat(
        [
            real_background.sample(n=n_real, random_state=42),
            external_background.sample(n=n_external, random_state=42),
        ]
    )

    # Combine balanced datasets
    balanced_df = pd.concat([balanced_background, non_background_samples])

    # Shuffle the dataset
    balanced_df = balanced_df.sample(frac=1, random_state=42).reset_index(drop=True)

    # Add the features column. The name is derived from the configured feature
    # type (mfcc_features / logmel_features / ...) because train_cnn.py and
    # train_xgboost.py auto-detect the single *_features column and use its
    # prefix as the MLflow feature_type.
    feature_params = params["feature_extraction"]
    features_dir = Path(feature_params["features_dir"])
    frames_per_ms = SAMPLING_RATE / feature_params["hop_length"] / 1000
    features_column = f"{feature_params['type']}_features"

    balanced_df[features_column] = balanced_df.parallel_apply(
        lambda row: get_features(
            row['chunk_start'],
            row['chunk_end'],
            row['audio_file_name'],
            features_dir,
            frames_per_ms,
        ),
        axis=1
    )

    chunks_per_label = balanced_df.groupby("label").size()
    chunks_per_label.to_csv("./data/data_quality/chunks_per_label.csv")

    chunk_data_quality = get_data_quality_metrics(balanced_df)
    with open("./data/data_quality/chunk_balanced_quality.json", "w") as f:
        json.dump(chunk_data_quality, f, indent=4)

    # Save balanced dataset
    balanced_df.to_hdf("./data/balanced_data.h5", key='data', index=False)

"""Dispatch to the configured training head.

The DAG needs one static `cmd` for the train_model stage so that a variant
is `dvc exp run -S training.head=...` rather than a branch with a different
dvc.yaml. This picks the head and validates it against the feature
representation before either trainer starts loading TensorFlow.
"""

import shutil

import yaml

from features import get_spec

MODEL_DIR = __import__("train_xgboost").MODEL_DIR

HEADS = ("cnn", "xgboost")


def check_compatible(head: str, feature_type: str) -> None:
    if head not in HEADS:
        raise SystemExit(
            f"unknown training.head {head!r}; known heads: {', '.join(HEADS)}"
        )
    spec = get_spec(feature_type)
    if head == "cnn" and not spec.keeps_time_axis:
        raise SystemExit(
            f"training.head 'cnn' needs a 2D (bins, frames) chunk, but feature "
            f"type {feature_type!r} pools the time axis away into a single "
            f"embedding vector. Use training.head 'xgboost' for {feature_type}."
        )


def main():
    with open("params.yaml", "r") as file:
        params = yaml.safe_load(file)

    head = params["training"]["head"]
    check_compatible(head, params["feature_extraction"]["type"])

    # A head switch must not leave the previous head's artifact sitting in
    # the output directory; dvc repro clears outs for us, a direct run does not.
    if MODEL_DIR.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(MODEL_DIR)
    MODEL_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    if head == "cnn":
        from train_cnn import main as train
    else:
        from train_xgboost import main as train

    train()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

1	"""Decide which audio chunks make up the training set -- before any features exist.
2	
3	This is the first half of what draw_data.py used to do. Splitting it out buys
4	two things:
5	
6	1. **Feature extraction stops being speculative.** It used to run over every
7	   file in every source, including all ~1900 external noise-pool files, and
8	   draw_data then sampled a few hundred background chunks out of that. Most
9	   of the extracted arrays were discarded -- cheap for log-mel, 769 MB for
10	   STFT. extract_features.py now reads this manifest and touches only the
11	   files a chunk actually references.
12	
13	2. **Sampling is shared across feature variants.** Nothing here depends on
14	   `feature_extraction`, so switching representation (or sweeping n_mels)
15	   reuses this stage's cache instead of re-deciding the split. Every variant
16	   therefore trains on exactly the same chunks, which is what makes the
17	   MLflow comparison between them mean anything.
18	
19	Output is data/chunk_manifest.csv, in final (shuffled) row order -- draw_data
20	just attaches features to it, so the ordering fed to the trainer is decided
21	here and only here.
22	"""
23	
24	import json
25	import pandas as pd
26	import yaml
27	from pandarallel import pandarallel
28	from pydub.utils import mediainfo
29	from tqdm import tqdm
30

32	from dataqualityutils import get_data_quality_metrics
33	from paths import DATA_QUALITY_DIR, MANIFEST_PATH
34	
35	
36	def split_background_draw(
37	    n_target: int, external_ratio: float, n_real_available: int, n_external_available: int
38	) -> tuple[int, int]:
39	    """How many background chunks to draw from real recordings vs the
40	    external noise pools. external_ratio is the desired external share; if
41	    one source can't fill its share (e.g. inbalance_ratio > 1 exhausts the
42	    real background chunks), the other tops it up.
43	    """
44	    n_external = int(round(n_target * external_ratio))
45	    n_real = n_target - n_external
46	
47	    if n_real > n_real_available:
48	        n_real = n_real_available
49	        n_external = min(n_target - n_real, n_external_available)
50	    elif n_external > n_external_available:
51	        n_external = n_external_available
52	        n_real = min(n_target - n_external, n_real_available)
53	
54	    return n_real, n_external
55	
56	
57	def build_annotations(params: dict) -> pd.DataFrame:
58	    annotated_data = pd.read_csv("./data/annotation_per_row_data.csv")
59	    # Synthetic front_doorbell samples from the augmentation stage (mixed
60	    # signal+noise at target SNRs) are appended as regular rows so they flow
61	    # through the same chunking/balancing logic as real annotations.
62	    augmented_data = pd.read_csv("./data/augmented_annotations.csv")
63	    annotated_data = pd.concat([annotated_data, augmented_data], ignore_index=True)
64	
65	    # External noise pool files (ESC-50, DEMAND) join as background rows so
66	    # the negative class also sees diverse non-Pi-mic noise, not just the
67	    # labeled recordings.
68	    external_data = external_background_rows(
69	        params["augmentation"]["external_noise_pools"]
70	    )
71	    annotated_data = pd.concat([annotated_data, external_data], ignore_index=True)
72	
73	    # Group key for leakage-safe train/val splitting downstream: augmented rows
74	    # already carry the source file of their signal chunk; real rows (no
75	    # split_group column in their CSV) group by their own file. Overlapping
76	    # sliding windows and SNR variants of one recording thus share a group.
77	    annotated_data["split_group"] = annotated_data["split_group"].fillna(
78	        annotated_data["audio_file_name"]
79	    )
80	    return annotated_data
81	
82	
83	def cut_into_chunks(annotated_data: pd.DataFrame, chunk_size: int, chunk_overlap: int):
84	    return pd.DataFrame(
85	        [
86	            row.to_dict()
87	            | {"chunk_start": chunk_start, "chunk_end": (chunk_start + chunk_size)}
88	            for _, row in annotated_data.iterrows()
89	            for chunk_start in range(
90	                int(row["start"] * 1000),  # convert to ms
91	                int(row["end"] * 1000) - chunk_size,
92	                chunk_overlap,
93	            )
94	        ]
95	    )
96	
97	
98	def balance_chunks(chunks: pd.DataFrame, params: dict) -> pd.DataFrame:
99	    background_samples = chunks[chunks["label"] == "background"]
100	    # TODO try imputations
101	    non_background_samples = chunks[chunks["label"] != "background"]
102	
103	    # Randomly sample from background class relative to the minority class
104	    # size (inbalance_ratio > 1 means more background than positives). Real
105	    # and external background are drawn separately so the huge external
106	    # pools can't crowd out the deployed-mic recordings.
107	    n_background_target = int(len(non_background_samples) * params["inbalance_ratio"])
108	    real_background = background_samples[background_samples["noise_pool"].isna()]
109	    external_background = background_samples[background_samples["noise_pool"].notna()]
110	    n_real, n_external = split_background_draw(
111	        n_background_target,
112	        params["external_background_ratio"],
113	        len(real_background),
114	        len(external_background),
115	    )
116	    if n_real + n_external < n_background_target:
117	        print(
118	            f"Warning: only {n_real + n_external} background chunks available, "
119	            f"target was {n_background_target}"
120	        )
121	    balanced_background = pd.concat(
122	        [
123	            real_background.sample(n=n_real, random_state=42),
124	            external_background.sample(n=n_external, random_state=42),
125	        ]
126	    )
127	
128	    balanced_df = pd.concat([balanced_background, non_background_samples])
129	    # Shuffle here rather than downstream: this is the row order the trainer
130	    # ultimately sees, and it must not depend on the feature variant.
131	    return balanced_df.sample(frac=1, random_state=42).reset_index(drop=True)

1	"""Export the trained CNN as a full-integer int8 TFLite model for the ESP32-S3.
2	
3	Two things make this more than a format conversion:
4	
5	1. **Normalization is baked into the graph.** train_cnn.py stores per-mel-bin
6	   mean/std in cnn_normalization.npz and applies them outside the model. Here
7	   they become a Rescaling layer in front of the trained network, so the
8	   firmware's C frontend only has to produce log-mel energies -- everything
9	   after that is the interpreter's job. One less place for train/serve skew.
10	
11	2. **The export is gated on int8 val F1.** Full-integer post-training
12	   quantization can quietly destroy a model that looks fine in float. The
13	   stage recomputes the same leakage-safe split train_cnn.py used, scores the
14	   int8 interpreter on the val fold, and fails if F1 drops by more than
15	   export.max_f1_drop.
16	
17	Outputs models/doorbell_int8.tflite (for reference/testing), the equivalent
18	C array in models/doorbell_model_data.cc (compiled into the firmware), and
19	models/tflite_metrics.json.
20	"""
21	
22	import hashlib
23	import json
24	import os
25	import shutil
26	from pathlib import Path
27	
28	import mlflow
29	import numpy as np
30	import tensorflow as tf
31	import yaml
32	from tensorflow import keras
33	
34	from paths import DATA_FILE, EXPORT_DIR
35	from train_cnn import MODEL_PATH, load_dataset, prepare_split
36	from train_xgboost import (
37	    MLFLOW_EXPERIMENT_NAME,
38	    compute_metrics,
39	    get_git_branch,
40	)
41	
42	NORMALIZATION_PATH = MODEL_PATH.with_name("cnn_normalization.npz")
43	TFLITE_PATH = EXPORT_DIR / "doorbell_int8.tflite"
44	C_ARRAY_PATH = EXPORT_DIR / "doorbell_model_data.cc"
45	# Outside EXPORT_DIR: it is a dvc metrics file (cache: false), and it is
46	# written on the skip path too, where EXPORT_DIR holds no model at all.
47	METRICS_PATH = Path("./models/tflite_metrics.json")
48	
49	C_ARRAY_VAR = "g_doorbell_model_data"
50	
51	
52	def build_export_model(trained: keras.Model, mean: np.ndarray, std: np.ndarray):
53	    """Prepend per-bin normalization so the graph consumes raw log-mel.
54	
55	    mean/std come from normalization_stats() with shape (n_bins, 1, 1), which
56	    broadcasts over the (batch, n_bins, n_frames, 1) input.
57	    """
58	    inputs = keras.Input(shape=trained.input_shape[1:], name="logmel")
59	    x = keras.layers.Rescaling(
60	        scale=(1.0 / std).astype(np.float32),
61	        offset=(-mean / std).astype(np.float32),
62	        name="normalize",
63	    )(inputs)
64	    outputs = trained(x)
65	    return keras.Model(inputs, outputs, name="doorbell_int8_export")
66	
67	
68	def convert_int8(model: keras.Model, representative: np.ndarray) -> bytes:
69	    """Full-integer PTQ. int8 in and out so no float ops remain for TFLM."""
70	    converter = tf.lite.TFLiteConverter.from_keras_model(model)
71	    converter.optimizations = [tf.lite.Optimize.DEFAULT]
72	    converter.target_spec.supported_ops = [tf.lite.OpsSet.TFLITE_BUILTINS_INT8]
73	    converter.inference_input_type = tf.int8
74	    converter.inference_output_type = tf.int8
75	
76	    def representative_dataset():
77	        for sample in representative:
78	            yield [sample[np.newaxis, ...].astype(np.float32)]
79	
80	    converter.representative_dataset = representative_dataset
81	    return converter.convert()
82	
83	
84	def tflite_predict(tflite_model: bytes, X: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
85	    """Run the int8 interpreter sample by sample, returning float scores."""
86	    interpreter = tf.lite.Interpreter(model_content=tflite_model)
87	    interpreter.allocate_tensors()
88	    inp = interpreter.get_input_details()[0]
89	    out = interpreter.get_output_details()[0]
90	
91	    in_scale, in_zero = inp["quantization"]
92	    out_scale, out_zero = out["quantization"]
93	
94	    scores = np.empty(len(X), dtype=np.float32)
95	    for i, sample in enumerate(X):
96	        quantized = np.clip(
97	            np.round(sample / in_scale + in_zero), -128, 127
98	        ).astype(np.int8)
99	        interpreter.set_tensor(inp["index"], quantized[np.newaxis, ...])
100	        interpreter.invoke()
101	        raw = interpreter.get_tensor(out["index"])[0, 0]
102	        scores[i] = (float(raw) - out_zero) * out_scale
103	    return scores
104	
105	
106	def largest_activation_bytes(tflite_model: bytes) -> int:
107	    """Biggest intermediate tensor, as an int8 arena sanity check.
108	
109	    Not the arena size itself -- TFLM's real requirement depends on its
110	    allocation planner and has to be confirmed on device -- but this is the
111	    number that decides internal SRAM vs PSRAM.
112	    """
113	    interpreter = tf.lite.Interpreter(model_content=tflite_model)
114	    interpreter.allocate_tensors()
115	    return max(
116	        int(np.prod(d["shape"])) * np.dtype(d["dtype"]).itemsize
117	        for d in interpreter.get_tensor_details()
118	        if len(d["shape"]) > 0
119	    )
120	
121	
122	def write_c_array(data: bytes, path: Path, var_name: str) -> None:
123	    """Emit an xxd-style C array plus its header, for the firmware build.
124	
125	    The array is 16-byte aligned because TFLM requires the flatbuffer to be
126	    aligned before it will parse it in place.
127	    """
128	    lines = [
129	        "// Generated by src/export_tflite.py -- do not edit.",
130	        "//",
131	        f"// int8 doorbell classifier, {len(data)} bytes.",
132	        "",
133	        f'#include "{path.with_suffix(".h").name}"',
134	        "",
135	        f"alignas(16) const unsigned char {var_name}[] = {{",
136	    ]
137	    for offset in range(0, len(data), 12):
138	        chunk = ", ".join(f"0x{byte:02x}" for byte in data[offset : offset + 12])
139	        lines.append(f"    {chunk},")
140	    lines.append("};")
141	    lines.append(f"const unsigned int {var_name}_len = {len(data)};")
142	    lines.append("")
143	    path.write_text("\n".join(lines))
144	
145	    guard = path.with_suffix(".h").name.upper().replace(".", "_") + "_"
146	    path.with_suffix(".h").write_text(
147	        "\n".join(
148	            [
149	                "// Generated by src/export_tflite.py -- do not edit.",
150	                "",
151	                f"#ifndef {guard}",
152	                f"#define {guard}",
153	                "",
154	                f"extern const unsigned char {var_name}[];",
155	                f"extern const unsigned int {var_name}_len;",
156	                "",
157	                f"#endif  // {guard}",
158	                "",
159	            ]
160	        )
161	    )
162	
163	
164	def skip(reason: str) -> None:
165	    """Leave the declared outputs in a valid, self-explaining state.
166	
167	    The stage is part of the default DAG so that every candidate model is
168	    scored after quantization, not before -- a variant that wins in float32
169	    and collapses in int8 is the wrong winner. But only the CNN head
170	    produces something convertible, so non-CNN runs record why there is no
171	    model here rather than failing the pipeline.
172	    """
173	    EXPORT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
174	    (EXPORT_DIR / "SKIPPED.json").write_text(
175	        json.dumps({"skipped": True, "reason": reason}, indent=4)
176	    )
177	    METRICS_PATH.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
178	    METRICS_PATH.write_text(json.dumps({"skipped": 1}, indent=4))
179	    print(f"export skipped: {reason}")
180	
181	
182	def main():
183	    with open("params.yaml", "r") as file:
184	        params = yaml.safe_load(file)
185	    export_params = params["export"]
186	
187	    if EXPORT_DIR.exists():
188	        shutil.rmtree(EXPORT_DIR)
189	
190	    head = params["training"]["head"]
191	    if head != "cnn":
192	        skip(f"training.head is {head!r}; int8 TFLite export needs the cnn head")
193	        return
194	
195	    # load_dataset -> prepare_data already appends the channel axis, so X is
196	    # (n, n_mels, n_frames, 1) here.
197	    X, y, le, feature_type, groups = load_dataset(params)
198	    train_idx, test_idx, _ = prepare_split(
199	        X, y, groups, params["training"]["test_size"]
200	    )
